items.title: A laptop-sized model that nearly matches frontier AI at analog chip design
items.explainer: SLIC is a training method where a small language model of a few billion parameters first imitates design demonstrations from a large model, then practices alone with reinforcement learning: it guesses circuit parameters, runs a simulator, checks the result and refines. Because the simulator gives a verifiable score, the model learns from real outcomes rather than opinions. MIT reports it came close to a flagship model's results while using a fraction of the compute.
items.why: It is a clear case that a small, private, specialised model can beat paying for the biggest one when the task has a checkable answer.

items.title: 7 percent of college students now get emotional support from AI chatbots
items.explainer: The Healthy Minds Study surveyed 67,477 students at 107 colleges and asked about chatbots for the first time. Seven percent said they had received counseling or emotional support from a chatbot like ChatGPT, and a co-author calls that likely an underestimate. The same survey shows depression and anxiety easing slightly.
items.why: Students are already using AI for more than homework, which belongs in any campus AI guidance conversation.

tryThisWeek.title: Grade an AI with a checkable answer
tryThisWeek.steps: Pick one task from your teaching that has a verifiable right answer, such as transposing a chord chart or fixing a set of verb tenses. Run it through a small free model and a large one, then score both against your key. Note where the small one is good enough.

lead.title: The small model that learned by running the simulator
lead.dek: MIT researchers trained a few-billion-parameter model to design analog circuits nearly as well as a flagship model, and it runs on a laptop.
paragraphs: SLIC, short for Small LM Iterating on Circuits, starts by having a large model produce demonstrations of the design process. The small model imitates those, then practices alone: it guesses component values, runs a circuit simulation, reads the result and tries again.

That loop is reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards. The simulator, not a human or another model, says whether a design meets its targets, so the small model gets honest feedback thousands of times. MIT says the model is several thousand times smaller than trillion-parameter frontier models and came close to matching the latest GPT model.

Because it runs locally, a chip company can keep its design and foundry data in house. The model also explains its choices in plain language, so engineers can follow and check its reasoning. The paper will be presented at NeurIPS 2026.
lead.against: The article reports no accuracy or cost figures, only that SLIC came close to a flagship model, and analog design has a precise simulator as a judge, which most real tasks lack.
lead.watch: Whether the same recipe of imitation plus a verifiable checker spreads to other fields with automatic graders, such as code, music theory drills or grammar exercises.
lead.ask: Which of your course tasks has an answer a machine could check, and would a small local model be enough for it?

graph.title: Campus mental health, a decade on
graph.tease: The Healthy Minds Study surveyed 67,477 students at 107 colleges in 2025 to 2026.
graph.question: Compared with a decade ago (2015 to 2016), how has the share of students with depression symptoms changed?
graph.reveal: Depression symptoms fell from 37 to 34 percent this year but remain about 9 points above 2015 to 2016. One good year is real progress, not a return to baseline.
graph.caveat: Large self-report survey; the 2015-16 figure is reported as approximate, and campuses in the sample vary by year.

argue.claim: If 7 percent of students already turn to chatbots for emotional support, colleges should write guidance for that use instead of pretending it is not happening.
argue.context: The Healthy Minds Study asked about chatbot support for the first time this year, and its authors think 7 percent undercounts it.
